messages:
sana: FYI — vendor released a security patch that touches the NVIDIA driver userland and some CUDA runtime libs. CVE summary from the feed below. Thinking we should plan a staged rollout across Dedicated pools and run compatibility validation against our CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL matrix.

devsec-bot: [CVE-2026-XXXX] libnvrtc/libraries: privilege escalation via crafted shader, vendor patch 554. Driver package nv-driver-554.10 and CUDA 12.2.1 runtime patch recommended. Severity: High. Affected: driver >= 530, runtime variants.

eric: Thanks. Can we get an inventory of hosts with driver < 554? I can script a canary rollout. Also need to confirm our docker images that bundle CUDA runtime — some use cudnn9, some use cudnn8.

maria: Quick notes: 1) Drivers that change ABI may force kernel module rebuilds (DKMS). 2) NCCL minor versions sometimes require matching CUDA minor. We'll need smoke tests for all three: driver + CUDA runtime + cuDNN + NCCL.

raj: I'm on the nightly inference tests — I can add a focused matrix run (a tiny batch) that exercises multi-GPU allreduce (NCCL), single-GPU conv (cuDNN), and a torch.jit compile path (CUDA runtime). If those pass we can be confident.

sana: Good. Proposal: 1) Blocklist user-facing clusters for immediate patching window next Tues. 2) Pick 2 canary hosts per pool (low-utilization). 3) Run validation matrix: nvidia-smi check, runtime smoke, small ML workload + perf baseline. 4) If green, roll 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m wait and health checks.

eric: Script snippets I used before:
```bash
# quick driver/runtime check
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv,noheader
python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.backends.cudnn.version())"
# container runtime check
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.2.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi
```
I'll add NCCL test: run the small allreduce test from nccl-tests.

maria: Also remember: Dedicated private deployments have our private kernel patch for an old distro. We must validate kernel module build step:
```bash
# DKMS flow
DKMS autoinstall --verbose
modprobe nvidia
journalctl -u dkms -n 200
```
If module build fails we need to fallback to the previous driver and abort rollout.

sana: Ops notes and audit: please log the rollout actions to the audit trail (RBAC action record). For Private customers, add a KMS key-rotated marker in the deployment notes only if we touch persistent artifacts (we don't plan to rotate keys now). Also tag all commits/rollouts with the CVE id.

eric: I'll create the canary playbook and a smoke test job in CI (eng-ml/nightly will get extended matrix). For on-prem we'll run the same tests via the private CI runner.

raj: One more thing — compatibility table to confirm:
- driver 554.x -> works with CUDA 12.2.1 runtime
- cuDNN 9.x -> validated, cuDNN 8 still used by some images (need to test)
- NCCL 2.18 -> expected, but run NCCL tests on multi-GPU nodes

sana: Plan ack. Eric, please post the canary playbook link once created. Maria/raj, note failure modes and exact log grep rules (e.g., "NVRM: Xid" and NCCL hang stacks) so we can auto-fail rollouts.

eric: will do — will also add automated rollback if kernel module build fails or if the perf regress >10% for the smoke jobs.

maria: I'll add the audit logging keys to the rollout doc: operator, run id, cluster, canary hosts, CVE id. Use the existing audit schema.

sana: thanks all. tagging this thread with :shield: and creating a follow-up ticket in Security backlog with checklist.

devsec-bot: Ticket created: SEC-1342 "NVIDIA driver CVE-2026-XXXX — canary rollout + compatibility validation". Assigned: eric, maria, raj. Due: 2026-03-30.
